chapter: Cecilia, Elvin Jones and jazz education
title: Last night's band: Dave Gibson, Earl May, Danny Mixon
summary: He and Brower discuss his current rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You had a pretty interesting drummer last night.
Dave Gibson, yeah.
I’d only heard him in a big band setting. Didn’t know that he played like that.
Yeah, he’s good in big or small groups. He’s strong, steady, swings hard, and imaginative, intelligent approach. He’s got everything that you need in a drummer. He’s got that power too.
Lots of power. He was very relaxed last night, but he brought some thunder, I thought.
Oh, yeah.
Was that a working band?

That is a working band. The bassist, believe it or not, is a sub for the regular bassist, who’s Earl May, but Gerald Cannon is the number one sub. When he’s there, it sounds like he’s the bassist with the group.
He had a different concept than Earl May, though. I can’t imagine Earl would have played the same things he would have played.
No, he wouldn’t. Earl is mostly a section player. He doesn’t play too many solos.
Rock. He’s a rock.
Yeah, he is a rock. So Gerald Cannon just does it all. He plays with the section, and he’s a wonderful soloist.
Danny Mixon was -­
Yeah, he’s the little orchestra in ten fingers.
Yeah, he dropped three or four -- made three jokes in every solo he took.
Yeah, he’s what we call the quote master.
Yeah, name that tune.
Right, name that tune [laughs].
I think Vanny Cook was comparing it to the way that Dexter used to do that in the course of his things, making all these references.
Yeah.
